blocks.text: Lots and land in East Burnaby

items.t: Burnaby Housing Authority — 10th Avenue and Newcombe Street (New Westminster edge). REZONING APPLICATION, rental, excluded from every count: the Burnaby Housing Authority (a municipal corporation established by the City of Burnaby) has submitted a rezoning application for a property at 10th Avenue and Newcombe Street with plans for 204 new affordable and market rental homes in two six-storey buildings with patios, community gardens and landscaped green spaces. Purpose-built rental by application — nothing here is a lot, a strata unit or a presale offering on this evidence.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around East Burnaby

items.t: Nearby areas: Edmonds and Highgate west and south-west, Cariboo and The Crest within the east side, South Slope south-west, and the City of New Westminster across 10th Avenue / the eastern border.

Main roads: Canada Way, Kingsway, Edmonds Street and 10th Avenue east–west, with 6th Street, 2nd Street and Cariboo Road running north–south toward Lougheed Highway and New Westminster. Transit: Edmonds Station (Expo Line) serves the west side; route 116 runs between Metrotown Station and Edmonds Station via Imperial, Sussex, Marine Drive, Marine Way, Byrne Road, Southridge Drive, Griffiths Drive and 18th Avenue.

Civic anchors: Robert Burnaby Park (creeks and streams throughout, over half its area critical wildlife habitat; 3 tennis courts and 10 pickleball courts with a practice wall); Rosemary Brown Recreation Centre, 7789 18th Street (2 NHL-sized rinks); Edmonds Community Centre, 7433 Edmonds Street, at the west edge; Tommy Douglas Library is the branch serving this quadrant. Nearest hospital: Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St, north-west across the city; Edmonds Urgent and Primary Care Centre at #201-7315 Edmonds St, at the west side.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in East Burnaby

items.t: Habitat diligence: over half of Robert Burnaby Park is critical wildlife habitat and restoration work runs through it — for park- and creek-edge lots, check watercourse setbacks and the restoration project's trail closures early.

If a parcel is in the ALR: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified. On ALR land the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is allowed only inside it, and an extra residence can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha). For farm class, BC Assessment looks for farm income of $10,000 a year on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8 to 4 ha, and $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha; applications are due by October 31.

blocks.text: Good to know about East Burnaby

items.t: The quadrant is being replanted while you buy in it: the City's Robert Burnaby Park restoration removes invasive species and plants 3,000 new trees, with some trails and areas closed during the work — a park-edge lot's outlook and access change over the project, in the improving direction, on the City's own description.

The east side's newest plan layer is dated March 2025: the Edmonds Community Plan was officially adopted that month for the town-centre part of the quadrant, and the Burnaby 2050 OCP (adopted December 9, 2025) now takes precedence over older community-plan maps where they conflict — check both layers for a town-centre-edge lot.

The City is its own landlord at the border: the 204-home project at 10th Avenue and Newcombe Street is the Burnaby Housing Authority's application — a municipal corporation's rental project, part of a two-project announcement totalling 387 new rental homes — so the quadrant's most visible "new development" adds rental supply, not purchasable land or strata.

blocks.text: East Burnaby home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

25 houses sold in East Burnaby with a median price of $1,612,000 (the middle half sold between $1,445,000 and $2,150,000), taking a median of 26 days to sell at 95.5% of the last list price; 4% sold above list. They had a median $592 per square foot, a median year built of 1991 and a median lot of 6,370 square feet. 9 duplexes sold in East Burnaby with a median price of $1,735,000 (the middle half sold between $1,480,000 and $1,866,667), taking a median of 24 days to sell at 97.1% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $675 per square foot and a median year built of 2025.

The east side's large forested park — the City describes many creeks and streams running through it and over half its area as critical wildlife habitat, and is restoring it with invasive-species removal and 3,000 new trees; its courts are listed at 3 tennis and 10 pickleball.
